source: Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture, HORDI tomato crop guide

entries.content: Tomato generally grows well in soil with pH 5.5 to 7.5; organic matter supports better growth.
Avoid excessive watering during dry periods because rapid changes in water availability can contribute to fruit cracking.
Early blight can produce dark lesions with concentric ring patterns on tomato leaves, stems, or fruit.
confirmation_questions: Do the spots contain ring-like circles?
Did symptoms begin on older lower leaves?

entries.content: Late blight may begin on older lower leaves as water-soaked grey-green spots that darken; white growth may appear on the leaf underside.
confirmation_questions: Is white growth visible beneath a fresh lesion?

entries.content: Target spot may cause circular dark-brown lesions with concentric patterns and a yellow halo; severe cases can cause leaves to yellow and collapse.
Powdery mildew may show light-green to yellow areas on the upper leaf surface and white powdery growth underneath.
confirmation_questions: Can the white powdery growth be seen on the lower surface?

entries.content: Keep young tomato fields free of weeds, especially roughly three to six weeks after transplanting, and weed before fertilizer application.
